evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep said 'That should take about five to ten minutes then he'll be able to build an accurate code you can depend on, sounds good' — framing present but stated as five to ten minutes (not the script's ten to fifteen), and the rep did wait for a yes before continuing. Partial because time-box slightly off and 'code' appears to be a misstatement for 'quote.'
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Jeremia Goree), moving day (Friday), route (Cedar Park to storage at 78747, with secondary stop to house on Laughlin Lane), size (1528 sq ft, single story, one-bedroom equivalent).
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked 'What are your biggest concerns or any is there any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' — but this came after the rep had already asked 'what are removing are we moving has an appointment?' and stated the property type. Technically probing had begun.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Rep asked 'Do you need help in packing?' and customer declined.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asked 'And how many number of boxes are we moving?' Customer answered 'Maybe a dozen.'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provided: 'typical one story house would normally takes two movers between six to eight hours'; then personalized: 'in your case... less than an hour away... only unloading two items... estimated time is between five and a half to six and a half hours estimated cost... would be $1,518.' Both anchor and personalization present.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Trip fee ($75) disclosed upfront. Rate framing ($104/hr per mover), 2.5-hour minimum, fifteen-minute increments, and 'no hidden fees of any type' all stated. Both present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asked 'Does that feel fair?' After pricing, jumped directly to availability and rate-lock messaging.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep stated: 'if you cannot make it to the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' Covers discount terms in recognizable form.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep stated: 'we have no worry damage coverage included on the already rate... We will provide up to 2000 dollars per move... to repair, replace and reimbursed for your items.' Covers $2,000, included in rate (no add-on), and no mention of deductible. Full delivery of the promise.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep never asked 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent. No loop-closing after the Two Promises section.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep did not ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any variant. No final concerns check occurred.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asked 'that said it actually believe that we the best move-in town would you like our help with your move' — plainly asked with no softening or out offered. Garbled phrasing but unmistakably an explicit ask.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Customer declined the move ('I'm gonna have to pass') citing price. Rep offered to email the quote; customer agreed. No booking details were confirmed because no booking was made. Partial credit at best would apply only if a booking had been attempted; here it is none.

top_strength: Rep gathered comprehensive logistics details across three stops (origin, secondary destination, storage) including property type, parking, access concerns, item specifics, walking distances, and storage specifications — full discovery picture for accurate quoting.
coaching_note: Rep needs to pause after stating the estimate and ask 'Does that feel fair?' with genuine silence before moving forward; this anchors customer buy-in and creates space for objections rather than losing the deal to sticker shock without attempting recovery.
